sections.title: The verb faire (to do, to make)

grammar_rules.title: Conjugation of aller (to go) in the present
grammar_rules.summary: Irregular: je vais, tu vas, il/elle/on va, nous allons, vous allez, ils/elles vont.
grammar_rules.explanation: Aller is an irregular 3rd group verb despite its -er ending. It is used for movement and forming the immediate future (futur proche).

steps: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont

grammar_rules.title: The immediate future (futur proche): aller + infinitive
grammar_rules.summary: Conjugated aller in present + infinitive of action verb expresses 'going to do something'.
grammar_rules.explanation: Formed with the present tense of aller followed by the infinitive: 'Je vais partir' (I am going to leave). In the negative, ne... pas surrounds aller: 'Je ne vais pas partir'.

grammar_rules.title: Conjugation of venir (to come) in the present
grammar_rules.summary: Irregular: je viens, tu viens, il/elle/on vient, nous venons, vous venez, ils/elles viennent.
grammar_rules.explanation: Venir and tenir (and all their compounds: devenir, revenir, prévenir, maintenir, retenir) follow the same conjugation pattern.

steps: viens, viens, vient, venons, venez, viennent

grammar_rules.title: The immediate past (passé récent): venir de + infinitive
grammar_rules.summary: Conjugated venir in present + de + infinitive expresses 'having just done something'.
grammar_rules.explanation: Use venir in the present followed by 'de' (or 'd'') and the infinitive of the verb to express an action that just happened: 'Je viens de manger' (I just ate / I have just eaten).

common_mistakes.wrong: Je viens manger (meaning I just ate)
common_mistakes.explanation: Without 'de', it means 'I am coming to eat'.

grammar_rules.title: Conjugation of faire (to do, to make) in the present
grammar_rules.summary: Irregular: je fais, tu fais, il/elle/on fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils/elles font.
grammar_rules.explanation: Notice the irregular 2nd person plural 'vous faites' and 3rd person plural 'ils font', and the pronunciation of 'nous faisons' [nufəzõ].

steps: je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font

notes: One of only three verbs taking -tes with vous (être -> vous êtes, faire -> vous faites, dire -> vous dites).

common_mistakes.explanation: Vous form is irregular: vous faites.

grammar_rules.title: The causative construction: faire + infinitive
grammar_rules.summary: Conjugated faire + infinitive means 'to have something done' or 'to cause someone to do something'.
grammar_rules.explanation: When you have someone else perform an action or cause an event, use faire + infinitive: 'Je fais réparer ma voiture' (I am having my car repaired); 'Il fait rire ses amis' (He makes his friends laugh).

steps: Follow immediately with infinitive of action verb

notes: Object pronouns precede faire: 'Je la fais réparer'.

usage_notes: Very common multi-verb construction for picking someone up
